sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Bulk Export of Organic Dried Lycium and Herbal Botanicals

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic tradition) with specialist commercial statutes
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) investment protection and promotion agreements with third states
Luxembourg-China Double Taxation Agreement (1985, with subsequent amendments)
Luxembourg-United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1996, as amended by Protocol)
Luxembourg-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (2012, as amended)
Luxembourg-Netherlands Double Taxation Agreement (1963, as amended)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) provisions on free movement of goods, services, and capital

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 5 June 2020 on the practical operation of the RBE register; CSSF and FIU Luxembourg implementing guidelines; relevant provisions of the Law of 17 December 2020 on the fight against non-compliance with EU restrictive measures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document for each manager and beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home country competent authority or certified notary in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the document originates from an Apostille Convention contracting state; otherwise consular legalization at the Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct / criminal record extract for each director and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local criminal records authority in the country of nationality or habitual residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization depending on the issuing state's participation in the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or proof of lawful source of funds for the proposed initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or regulated financial institution of the investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature and, where issued in an Apostille Convention state, Hague Apostille; otherwise consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft articles of association / statuts of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg civil-law notary responsible for incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial deed executed before the Luxembourg notary and registered with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register; no apostille required for domestic notarial acts

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence on all shareholders, directors, and UBOs with a 25% or greater ownership interest or substantive control. Screening is required against the consolidated EU sanctions list, UN Security Council sanction lists, OFAC SDN list, Luxembourg FIU and CSSF watchlists, and publicly available domestic PEP databases. PEP status must be risk-rated in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12, and any PEP or sanctioned individual triggers mandatory reporting to the Luxembourg FIU (Cellule de Renseignements Financiers) and filing of STRs/SARs where applicable. The AML/CFT Law also requires ongoing monitoring of business relationships and source of funds verification for the initial share capital.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online platform at lbr.lu / rcs.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate name must be written in Latin-alphabet characters; Luxembourg official languages are French, German, and Luxembourgish, but the name may use a foreign language provided it is transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The SARL legal form must be indicated either by the full French expression 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or by the conventional abbreviation 'S.à r.l.' or 'SARL'. The name must be distinctive, not misleading, and must not conflict with existing RCS-registered names, protected trademarks, or names of public authorities.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fonds / Investment Fund / Fonds d'investissement alternatif
Office / Administration / Etat / Government / Royal or Sovereign references
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects the proposed name, the applicant receives a reasoned refusal through the online e-RCS filing interface. The applicant may, within one month of the refusal, file a formal administrative appeal before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) under the general civil procedural rules applicable to RCS decisions. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately submit an amended name proposal; the 30-day name reservation/window cannot be extended, so a fresh clearance and reservation request must be submitted for any revised corporate name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible for initial filing purposes only. The SARL must have a real registered office (siège) in Luxembourg, being either owned or leased premises appropriate for the company's business. A virtual office address supplied by a licensed service provider may satisfy the RCS address filing requirement, but it does not establish sufficient commercial substance for VAT, customs, transfer pricing, and general anti-abuse rules. For the dried goji berry and herbal wholesale business, the customs and tax authorities expect a demonstrable administrative presence, including a letterbox agreement, local management capacity, and evidence of decision-making within Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate for a low-risk wholesale trading entity; estimated 5–10% annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection by the RCS, Luxembourg VAT administration, or customs authorities, particularly if there are anomalies in import/export declarations, VAT filings, or chain transaction documentation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS name clearance and availability check through Luxembourg Business Registers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory e-tariff of the Luxembourg official trade register

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of articles of association (statuts) and preparation of the notarial deed of incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notary fee schedule / market benchmark for a standard SARL deed with minimum capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the SARL with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration tariff for a Société à Responsabilité Limitée

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory publication in the Electronic Collection of Companies and Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice / Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication fee per page/entry under Luxembourg company law

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of beneficial owner (UBO) information with the Register of Beneficial Owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign identification, good conduct, and source-of-funds documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Luxembourg diplomatic or consular posts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official Hague Apostille fee schedule / consular legalization tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC and PEP/sanctions screening package for directors and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary and authorized AML/CFT compliance service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional due diligence fee benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as modernized by the Law of 23 September 2016; SARL-specific provisions at Articles 710-1 to 710-25 (incorporation deed, share capital, shares, management by gérant, and statutory audit regime); ancillary filing rules under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the trade and companies register (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés — RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the supervisory authority of the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg); post-registration publication in the Electronic Collection of Companies and Associations (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations — RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (incorporation deed) executed either as a notarized authentic deed where a contribution in kind, real-estate contribution, or statutory-auditor report is involved, or as a private deed (acte sous seing privé) for a purely cash-subscribed SARL; the deed embeds the annexed articles of association (statuts) and is filed at the RCS with a subsequent mandatory excerpt in the RESA.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum statutory share capital is EUR 1.00 (one euro) under Article 710-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended; the subscribed capital must be fully paid up in cash before incorporation and deposited into a blocked escrow account (compte bancaire bloqué) opened in the name of the SARL at a Luxembourg or EU/EEA credit institution; the bank's blocked-funds certificate (attestation de blocage) must accompany the RCS filing and the funds are released only upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: 1. The sole shareholder acknowledges that [Company Name] SARL was incorporated by deed dated [date] with a share capital of EUR [amount], fully subscribed and paid up into the blocked account. 2. Resolved to confirm the allotment of [number] shares to [Shareholder Name]. 3. Resolved to fix the registered office at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and to accept the execution of the lease. 4. Resolved to appoint [Manager Name] as manager (gérant) of the company with sole signature authority. 5. Resolved to instruct the manager to open the company's operating bank accounts and to file the incorporation deed, blocked-funds certificate, and related declarations with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register. 6. Resolved to register for VAT, business establishment, and beneficial-owner formalities as required by law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of the Corporate Name and Issuance of the Negative Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS e-Filing Portal (www.lbr.lu; rcs.lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the LBR portal, conduct an availability search and submit three ranked proposed names together with the corporate-object description; once cleared, the RCS issues the negative certificate (certificat de non-usage), which must be annexed to the incorporation deed within its validity window; a local agent may file on behalf of foreign shareholders.
required_dossiers: Three proposed corporate names in order of preference
Identity document of the applicant
Short description of the corporate object
Proof of payment of the name-search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Refusal of a name: amend the name list and re-file within five business days; disputes over confusing similarity may be cured by a letter of consent from the prior registrant; judicial appeal to the District Court within one month remains available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Blocked Escrow Account and Deposit of the Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg or EU/EEA credit institution chosen by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the draft statutes and the bank's standard corporate KYC questionnaire; the sole shareholder transfers the fully subscribed capital (statutory minimum EUR 1) into a blocked account opened in the name of the SARL; the bank issues the blocked-funds certificate (attestation de blocage) confirming that the funds are frozen until production of the RCS registration extract; the certificate must be dated within the period accepted by the notary or registry.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation deed and articles of association
Passport/ID and KYC documentation of each shareholder and of the gérant
Negative name certificate
Business plan and source-of-funds statement for AML purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the bank applies enhanced due diligence, supply sworn bank references and source-of-wealth declarations; if the application is declined, open the account at another Luxembourg or EU/EEA bank and adjust the notarial timeline; a certificate from any EU/EEA credit institution is acceptable if duly authenticated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Incorporation Deed and Statutory Articles (Acte Constitutif)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Luxembourg notary for contributions in kind, real-estate contributions, or statutory-auditor reports; otherwise execution by private deed (acte sous seing privé) of the sole shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize and approve the statutes with counsel; the incorporator executes the deed before a Luxembourg notary, or signs the private deed with annexes for cash-only SARLs; where contributions in kind occur, a statutory auditor's special report per Article 710-7 is mandatory and the deed must be notarial; the deed fixes share allotment, registered office, gérant, corporate object, and any permitted activities; remote incorporators may act through certified powers of attorney with apostilles or legalization.
required_dossiers: Final statutes (articles of association)
Negative certificate
Blocked-funds certificate
Passport copies and proof of residence of incorporators
Consent of the gérant and specimen signature
Certificate of non-conviction of the gérant, if relevant
Certified or apostilled powers of attorney for remote incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial queries are cured by filing amended statutory clauses and re-signing; if a remote mandate is challenged, produce a fresh, duly legalized power of attorney; a defective special report on contributions in kind may be reissued by the réviseur d'entreprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing with the RCS and Publication in the RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the LBR e-filing platform; publication in the RESA (Mémorial C)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the signed deed, annexed statutes, blocked-funds certificate, manager identification, and beneficial-owner data through the LBR e-file channel, or through the notary where notarization was used; pay the statutory registration fee online; the RCS verifies legality, allocates the sole registration number, and orders publication; the SARL acquires legal personality on registration; an official RCS extract is then obtainable for bank, tax, and licensing purposes.
required_dossiers: Signed incorporation deed and annexed statutes
Blocked-funds certificate
RCS electronic registration form
Identification and consent of the gérant
Beneficial-owner data for the initial RBE declaration
Proof of the registered-office domiciliation agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, cure it by filing a corrigendum within the notified deadline, generally 15 days, with payment of any additional fee; minor data errors are corrected by a rectification filing; a refusal of registration is appealable to the District Court within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry of Beneficial Owners (RBE) Filing and VAT/Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE register); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the initial beneficial-owner declaration within one month of RCS registration, identifying natural persons owning more than 25%; submit Form 600 to the AEDT within 15 days of commencing the commercial activity, or immediately where intra-EU acquisitions are expected; obtain the Luxembourg VAT number, noting that export sales to non-EU buyers are zero-rated subject to documentary evidence; corporate income tax and net-wealth tax files are created automatically by the AEDT, but the company must confirm its tax unit and provide bank details for refunds.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
RBE declaration form and supporting identification documents
VAT Form 600 and manager's identity document
Description of the dried-goji-berry and herbal export activity
Bank account certificate for tax refund purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: RBE late-filing penalties are avoided by filing within the one-month window or by submitting a written force-majeure explanation to the LBR; incorrect VAT data may be corrected through the myGuichet e-desks; tax disputes are appealable to the director of the AEDT and thereafter to the Administrative Tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Establishment Permit and Food/Export Operational Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy — Department for the Registration of Trades (Direction générale des classes moyennes); food-business registration through the Ministry of Health, Food Safety Division, and the Administration des services vétérinaires (ASTA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing wholesale and export activities, apply for the business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) under the amended Law of 2 September 2011, proving that the gérant holds the required professional qualification or that a duly qualified technical manager is employed; register the warehouse and handling premises as a food business operator under Regulation (EC) 852/2004; obtain the municipal commodo declaration for the storage facility; arrange health or phytosanitary certificates for third-country consignments of dried lycium and herbal botanicals; the permit application is filed after RCS registration and before first commercial operation.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Business establishment permit application form and fee receipt
Diplomas, certificates, or professional-experience evidence of the qualifying manager
Lease or ownership documents for the warehouse and registered office
HACCP plan and food-safety registration form
Phytosanitary and health certificate templates for export consignments
Fire-safety and structural certificates for the warehouse
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A refusal of the business permit can be cured by appointing a technically qualified gérant or engaging an authorized storage partner; food-safety objections may be cured by submitting an amended HACCP plan; administrative decisions remain appealable to the Administrative Tribunal within three months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy, General Directorate for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (Direction générale des classes moyennes) through the Department for the Registration of Trades; municipal Commodo authority of the commune where the warehouse is located for the operation of the storage facility
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business establishment permit for a trader (autorisation d'établissement pour activité commerciale) covering the wholesale distribution and international bulk export of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals, issued under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions of craftsman, trader, industrialist, and certain liberal professions.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity; coordinated with the municipal Commodo board for the storage site
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 3 activity (light warehousing and repackaging of dried botanicals): only a simplified commodo declaration (déclaration de classe 3) is required before the municipal Commodo board; a full environmental impact assessment report is not mandated under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment, provided the activity does not trigger the Annex IV thresholds for surface area, storage capacity, or hazardous-substance handling.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: domestic-type effluent only; any industrial discharge must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 July 2013 on industrial wastewater and requires prior authorization from the Administration de la gestion de l'eau. Emissions: negligible VOC emissions from dried plant material; airborne dust and botanical spores must remain below the occupational exposure limits set under Article 19 of the Labour Code. Waste: mandatory segregation of organic residues and packaging per the amended Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management; cross-border shipments of waste, if any, must follow Regulation (EC) 1013/2006. Product compliance: food traceability per Regulation (EC) 178/2002 and hygiene controls per Regulation (EC) 852/2004 apply to the dried goji berries and herbal botanicals.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and clearance certificate issued by the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours — CGDIS) covering extinguishers, emergency exits, and dry-storage fire risks; structural load certification by an approved engineering office for the warehouse slab, racking, and shelving; workplace occupational safety clearance by the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (Inspection du travail et des mines — ITM) under the amended Law of 17 June 1994 on safety and health at work, including the appointment of a safety coordinator where construction-phase obligations arise.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) through the MyGuichet.lu single official digital portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity must appoint a Luxembourg tax representative for VAT and direct tax purposes if it has no permanent establishment. For a local SARL, the entity is incorporated before a notary, registered with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), and automatically assigned a national business number (numéro national) and VAT number by the AEDT. The foreign entity must submit the standard registration form (Formulaire 106 VAT) via MyGuichet.lu or the Luxembourg registration desk, provide the notarized incorporation deed, articles of association, identity documents of directors/shareholders, proof of address, and RCS extract. The AEDT issues the VAT identification number (numéro d'identification TVA) upon verification, typically within two to four weeks; no minimum capital or residency conditions apply for the foreign-owned SARL beyond regulatory corporate requirements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg applies an entity-level corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) with no general check-the-box regime. However, certain elections are available: (a) a fully taxable Luxembourg SARL may elect to join a Luxembourg fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) with 95% or more owned resident subsidiaries for corporate income tax and municipal business tax purposes, effectively offsetting profits and losses; (b) qualifying entities may elect joint venture status under Article 175bis LIR; (c) a Luxembourg SARL may opt for the special VAT franchise (régime de la franchise) only below the small-enterprise threshold, and may elect to remain outside the VAT reverse-charge rules by registering; (d) hybrid mismatch elections are limited to aligning classification under Luxembourg domestic law and the relevant double tax treaty where the entity is fiscally transparent in another jurisdiction, but a Luxembourg SARL as a corporate entity is not eligible for pass-through treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Luxembourg imposes no general VAT registration threshold for businesses established in Luxembourg; any person carrying out taxable economic activity must register for VAT regardless of turnover. A non-established foreign supplier may be required to register from the first euro of taxable supplies in Luxembourg subject to the distance-selling thresholds under EU VAT rules (EUR 10,000 cross-border intra-EU distance sales threshold for non-established EU suppliers; non-EU suppliers must register without threshold for B2C supplies of electronically supplied services under the special schemes or the general reverse-charge rules may apply for B2B supplies).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently mandate a national e-invoicing clearance model for domestic B2B transactions. E-invoicing is permitted under EU Directive 2014/55/EU and the Luxembourg e-invoicing framework (Peppol BIS Billing 3.0), and invoices must be issued within the standard B2B 30-day deadline. There is no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory government API stamping, and no digital-fiscal-stamp requirement for standard agricultural or wholesale transactions. However, if the SARL uses certified billing software, the software must ensure data integrity and auditability; for cross-border supplies, the recapitulative statement (Intrastat and EC Sales List) must be filed electronically via the AEDT e-file system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Luxembourg to a non-EU destination qualify for the 0% VAT rate under Article 44 of the Luxembourg VAT Law (loi TVA) provided the goods are physically dispatched or transported outside the EU by the supplier or on behalf of the supplier within the statutory time frame (90 days from supply). The supplier must obtain and retain proof of export (justificatifs de transport/exportation). Offshore services (e.g., services related to goods exported outside the EU) may also qualify for zero-rating under the place-of-supply rules where the customer is established outside the EU or the services are directly related to exported goods. For the bulk wholesale export of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals under ISIC 4631, the zero-rating criterion is satisfied only if the SARL retains full documentary evidence that title passed to the non-EU buyer, the goods left the EU, and the export declaration matches the commercial invoice in quantity, value, and product description.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation via the Luxembourg Single Administrative Document or the electronic Customs Declaration System of the EU – ICS/ECS)
Bill of Lading (Airway Bill or CMR consignment note depending on the mode of transport)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT proof of payment or bank statement confirming receipt of funds from the foreign buyer)
Certificate of Origin (EUR.1 or non-preferential certificate where required)
Phytosanitary Certificate and Organic Certification (EU Organic Regulation 2018/848) for herbal botanicals
Proof of Logistics Contract with named transporter and route
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities may retrospectively deny zero-rating and reclassify the supply as taxable at the standard 17% VAT if the documentary evidence is incomplete or inconsistent. The taxpayer bears the burden of proof. Penalties for fraudulent export zero-rating claims include: (i) payment of the under-assessed VAT plus default interest at the statutory rate; (ii) an administrative fine of up to EUR 250,000 or 10% of the tax due where negligence exists; (iii) criminal sanctions for tax fraud under Article 16 of the Luxembourg Criminal Code and the General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung), including imprisonment up to five years and fines up to EUR 125,000; (iv) exclusion from VAT number validity and mandatory security deposit requirements for continued registration; and (v) liability of the managing director for the company's VAT debt. A clawback is not limited to the transaction in question — the authorities may extend audit scrutiny to all intra-EU and export sales, apply penalty interest, and dissolve the SARL for serious management failures.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); supervisory authority for credit institutions and payment/EMI institutions is the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. Luxembourg applies the EU Capital Movements Directive (88/361/EEC) and TFEU Art. 63; no exchange controls or approvals for current or capital transactions. Profit remittances are unrestricted; dividend payments may be subject to Luxembourg withholding tax (15% standard, 0% under participation exemption where conditions met, reduced under DTTs). For balance-of-payments statistics, transactions >EUR 12,500 must be reported to BCL using standard purpose codes, but this is a statistical filing duty, not a regulatory barrier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg has no surrender, repatriation, or conversion requirement for export proceeds. Exporters may retain currency balances in foreign-currency accounts held with Luxembourg banks or abroad.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)
KBL European Private Bankers S.A. (Quintet Private Bank (Europe) S.A.)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium with legal constraints. A Luxembourg-authorised or EEA-passported Electronic Money Institution (EMI) under PSD2 can be used for compartmentalised payment flows, but is not a viable sole treasury vehicle for a wholesale SARL engaged in physical commodity trade. Constraints: EMIs cannot pay interest, extend credit, or accept deposits; they face strict safeguarding obligations; trade finance instruments (LCs, guarantees) are not within the standard EMI licence. An offshore digital EMI (e.g. non-EEA) is generally not viable for primary settlement due to AML/KYC equivalence, CSSF supervision gap, and bank de-risking reluctance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted in principle under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 (amended) via video identification with eIDAS and secure signature, but most tier-1 banks require at least one authorised director (gérant) to attend an in-person interview at the category A (basic) onboarding stage, or to provide a notarised power of attorney with apostille plus a certified corporate KYC pack. For high-risk or non-EU ownership, physical presence is mandatory. Directors must submit a valid passport, proof of residential address, criminal record extract or equivalent, CV/BIOS, and source of funds and wealth statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner located in high-risk or tax-non-transparent jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized register of beneficial owners (Luxembourg RBE extract), sworn declarations of UBO, tax residency certificates, corporate organigram, source-of-wealth report from an independent auditor, and evidence of economic substance at the SARL (office lease, local payroll, management meetings).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction pattern for dried goji berries / herbal botanicals
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade finance documents: purchase contracts, commercial invoices, packing lists, ocean/airway bills, phytosanitary certificates, certificates of origin, U.S.-EU food safety compliance records (or equivalent), warehouse receipts, and customs declarations matching each shipment to a contractual purchase order.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Invoicing value misalignment (trade-based money laundering indicator)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party commodity pricing benchmark reports (e.g. Mintec, S&P Global Platts, or local organic produce exchange), market analysis from an approved chamber of commerce, independent appraiser valuation for each lot, and audit letter from a Chartered Accountant confirming arm's-length margin benchmarks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial deposit from an offshore fintech or third-party payment provider
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written explanation of payment chain, copies of the fintech's licence and regulatory registration, AML/CTF policies of the PSP, bank statements evidencing source of underlying funds, and legal undertaking that no cash or anonymous instruments are involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or politically exposed connection among shareholders or counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive PEP risk assessment, gap report from an AML advisory firm, evidence of commercial rationale for the PEP relationship, transaction monitoring and audit trail, and written approval from the bank's compliance committee.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder loans must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 with a BCL balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment (commonly 'S301 – Equity capital for a direct investment' or equivalent code as specified by the BCL statistical reporting circular). Verification: copy of the share subscription resolution, notarized incorporation deed, bank proof of funds from the remitting shareholder, and confirmation that the credit to the account in Luxembourg is not below the statutory minimum capital for an SARL. Transfers above EUR 12,500 must be reported to BCL by the Luxembourg receiving bank via the central reporting system; no prior authorisation is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement of international trade obligations, the preferred rails are: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct wire payments with mirrored invoice and transport documents retained in the bank's trade verification file; (ii) Commercial documentary letters of credit (LC) issued by the Luxembourg bank (UCP 600) for high-value shipments, especially where the overseas buyer requires bank assurance; (iii) SWIFT MT202/MT210 for cover payments between banks. All outbound disbursements require the standard supporting packet: purchase agreement, supplier invoice, bill of lading, customs declaration, and where applicable phytosanitary or conformity certificate. Payments to non-EU sanction-affected jurisdictions are blocked irrespective of trade documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright currency forwards (EUR/CNY, EUR/USD, EUR/INR) for committed trade cash flows
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referenced to non-convertible currencies (e.g. onshore CNY, INR) subject to bank counterparty credit limits
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for term-matching of export receivables and liability cash flows
FX options (vanilla and exotic) structured under MIFIR/MIFID II, used as hedge overlay only
FX spot contracts for immediate settlement of trade invoices or payroll
Money market deposits in foreign currency to minimise conversion frequency, held as treasury buffer

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approved annual accounts (comptes annuels) with directors' report and statutory auditor's report if required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within 6 months of financial year-end; RCS electronic deposit within 7 months of financial year-end (31 July for a calendar-year entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties from EUR 100 to EUR 500; repeated non-deposit may cause RCS to refer the SARL to the Public Prosecutor, with judicial dissolution or strike-off and director personal liability for formalities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Formulaire 100 and annexes) including municipal business tax details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD / Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year financial year, filed by 31 December of the following year; electronic filing via Connect; extension of up to 9 months may be requested
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to 10% of assessed tax, default interest of 0.6% per month, and possible ex officio assessment; prolonged non-filing does not directly trigger strike-off but exposes the entity to enforced collection and director liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than 31 December of the year following the relevant assessment year; same filing extension rules as the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.6% per month and late-filing penalty up to 10% of the net wealth tax due; persistent failure may result in enforced recovery from bank accounts or assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual exactness confirmation of beneficial owner (RBE) information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE / Ministry of Justice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the date communicated by the RBE (market practice for calendar-year entities: 31 March); any change in shareholding or ownership is additionally reportable within 1 month of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine from EUR 250 to EUR 1,250 per breach; intentional or repeated non-compliance may lead to criminal fines up to EUR 10,000 and imprisonment for directors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual periodical VAT reconciliation or annual VAT return where expressly authorised
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For approved annual VAT filing, declaration and settlement due by 31 May of the following year; for monthly or quarterly filers, the final-return deadline is 15 days after the period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to 10% of VAT due and monthly late interest; serious or persistent failure may constitute a criminal offence and result in suspension of the business licence

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent audit for a Luxembourg SARL when, in two consecutive financial years, any two of three thresholds are exceeded: balance sheet total above EUR 4,400,000; net turnover above EUR 8,800,000; average full-time employees above 50. Audit is also mandatory if the SARL is part of an EU group subject to consolidation, its activity is regulated, or shareholders controlling at least 25% of voting rights request the appointment of a réviseur d'entreprises.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2019 transposing Directive 2013/34/EU; Plan Comptable Normalisé). IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for consolidated financial statements but is not required for the standalone statutory annual accounts of an unlisted SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Luxembourg SARL must maintain an accurate RBE record identifying every holder of more than 25% of shares or voting rights and any ultimate beneficial interest. Each year, the SARL reviews and confirms the RBE data within the period fixed by Luxembourg Business Registers (commonly 31 March for calendar-year entities). Any share transfer that changes beneficial ownership must be filed with the RBE within 1 month of the transfer, and the old and new shareholders must be recorded in the statutory share register. A transfer is not opposable to the company or third parties until formal recording is completed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholders' and management board meetings
Register of Beneficial Owners and RBE confirmation file
Accounting books, vouchers and annual accounts file retained for 7 years

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 1,800 – 5,800 (Luxembourg registered office and corporate secretarial agent)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 4,500 – 12,000 depending on balance-sheet complexity and group-reporting obligations

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined corporate income tax, solidarity surcharge, and municipal business tax for Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard incentives include: 80% exemption on qualifying intellectual property income (IP regime), investment tax credit (8% for certain new tangible assets), and participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains. No specific sectoral incentives for wholesale trade.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1001 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu (Luxembourg's official e-filing portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Must be filed by 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end, unless extended by the tax administration (typically to 31 December upon request).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the company (name, address, registration number, tax ID).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Luxembourg tax ID and proof of permanent establishment if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the accounting period covered by the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (net profit before tax adjustments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income if resident; for non-residents, only Luxembourg-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses (e.g., fines, excessive interest, non-business entertainment).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back any expenses not deductible under Luxembourg tax law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt income (e.g., participation exemption dividends, IP income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty or domestic exemptions with supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply available loss carryforwards (indefinite, subject to change-of-ownership rules).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (e.g., investment tax credit, foreign tax credit).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute credits per Luxembourg rules; attach supporting schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of corporate income tax, solidarity surcharge, and municipal business tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply applicable rates; municipal rate varies by commune.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: €250 to €2,500 per month of delay, plus interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid tax. Intentional non-filing may lead to criminal penalties and director liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (standard rate), reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (if holding ≥10% for at least 12 months) or under a tax treaty (e.g., 5% or 0% depending on treaty).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the beneficial owner must submit a request for exemption or reduction via the Luxembourg tax administration (Form 105) and provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the residence state. The payer must withhold at the statutory rate unless a prior approval for reduced withholding is obtained. For EU directives, a self-declaration of eligibility is required.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose withholding tax on royalties or interest paid to non-residents, except for interest on profit-sharing loans (subject to 15% WHT). Treaty rates may apply but are generally 0% for royalties and interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if the entity's annual turnover exceeds €10 million or if related-party transactions exceed €1 million. Master File required if the group's consolidated turnover exceeds €50 million. Documentation must be prepared by the filing deadline.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) for entities engaged in geographically mobile activities (e.g., IP holding, financing). For a wholesale trading company, substance is evidenced by local management, employees, office premises, and decision-making. Failure to meet substance may lead to recharacterization and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, false invoicing, or artificial transfer pricing arrangements to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to €250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years. Civil penalties up to 200% of the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion. Travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox company with no real presence, no employees, no local management, or no physical office, while claiming treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, and imposition of 15% withholding tax on deemed dividends. Administrative fines up to €50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for unpaid taxes and penalties if they fail to ensure substance. In severe cases, criminal charges for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, reporting suspicious transactions, or maintaining proper records for cross-border payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million for legal entities, plus suspension of business license. Criminal prosecution of responsible officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can face imprisonment up to 5 years and personal fines up to €500,000 for AML violations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation or applying non-arm's length pricing in related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalties up to 10% of the adjustment, and interest on underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant pricing. In egregious cases, criminal tax evasion charges.
